paper.title_en: Amplitudes approach to spinning black hole scattering
paper.abstract_en: The monumental detection of gravitational waves by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration has ushered in a new era for precision studies of gravity. Notably, it has provided unprecedented insight into the complex dynamics of binary systems composed of massive, compact astrophysical objects such as neutron stars and black holes. This observational leap has called for equally impressive advances in our theoretical understanding of these gravitational two-body systems. Towards this direction, scattering amplitudes have remarkably emerged as a robust tool for precisely this purpose, allowing us to leverage the rich machinery of high-energy physics. In this thesis, we study the classical dynamics associated with the scattering of two black holes. Our overarching goal is to systematically include the effects of black hole spin—an important feature of real astrophysical systems—thereby describing the dynamics of Kerr black holes. To this end, we model Kerr black holes as massive point particles in finite-spin representations and compute their scattering dynamics perturbatively. In fact, this strategy introduces an ambiguity that mixes classical and quantum contributions, which we elegantly resolve using our spin interpolation method. Using this method, we obtain a completely novel classical amplitude for Kerr black hole scattering accurate to the quartic order in spin and at the third post-Minkowskian order. From this amplitude we extract the gauge-invariant radial action, enabling the computation of classical non-aligned-spin observables—such as the linear and angular impulses—using covariant Dirac brackets.Most excitingly, the classical amplitude we obtain exhibits a spin-shift symmetry: it remains invariant under a shift of the black hole spin by the momentum transfer in the scattering process. Motivated by this mysterious property, we examine the conserved quantities governing the scattering process and show that the dynamics of a probe black hole remains integrable at asymptotic infinity through the quartic order in probe spin. Finally, we show that the quartic-in-spin radial action, for a probe black hole in a Kerr background, at any order in perturbation theory is completely fixed by the aligned-spin dynamics, provided that it satisfies asymptotic integrability and spin-shift symmetry.
